title: Reflexive verbs and the daily routine
summary: Me levanto, te duchas, se acuesta: verbs you do to yourself.
focus: Reflexive pronouns and verbs in the present tense; llamarse
content:
## What a reflexive verb is

A reflexive verb has **-se** on the infinitive (*levantarse*, *ducharse*, *llamarse*) and takes a **reflexive pronoun** that matches the subject. The action falls back on the person doing it: *me levanto* = I get (myself) up.

| | pronoun | levantarse (to get up) |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **me** | me levanto |
| tú | **te** | te levantas |
| él / ella / usted | **se** | se levanta |
| nosotros/as | **nos** | nos levantamos |
| vosotros/as | **os** | os levantáis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **se** | se levantan |

The pronoun goes **before** the conjugated verb: *No me levanto temprano.*

## Llamarse

You already know *me llamo* (my name is, literally *I call myself*): *me llamo, te llamas, se llama, nos llamamos, os llamáis, se llaman*. *¿Cómo se llama tu hermano?*: What's your brother's name?

## The daily routine

| | |
|---|---|
| despertarse (e→ie) | to wake up: *me despierto* |
| levantarse | to get up |
| ducharse | to have a shower |
| lavarse (los dientes) | to wash (one's teeth) |
| vestirse (e→i) | to get dressed: *me visto* |
| desayunar | to have breakfast (not reflexive) |
| acostarse (o→ue) | to go to bed: *me acuesto* |
| dormirse (o→ue) | to fall asleep: *me duermo* |

*Me levanto a las siete, me ducho, desayuno y salgo a las ocho. Por la noche me acuesto a las once.*

Body parts take the article, not a possessive: *me lavo **las** manos*, not *mis manos*.

## With an infinitive

The pronoun can go before the first verb or attach to the infinitive: *Me voy a levantar* = *Voy a levantar**me***. Both are correct.

vocabulary.example_meaning: He has a shower in the morning.
He falls asleep on the sofa.

quiz.explanation: Yo takes the reflexive pronoun me.
hints: The reflexive pronoun that goes with yo.

quiz.prompt: Mi hermano ___ ducha por la noche.

quiz.explanation: Nosotros has no stem change: nos acostamos.
Body parts take the article with reflexive verbs: las manos.
Vestirse is e → i: me visto.
The pronoun goes before the first verb or attached to the infinitive, never in between.

quiz.prompt: Los niños ___ acuestan a las nueve.
___ a las ocho. (I have breakfast at eight.)

listening.text: Nos levantamos muy tarde los domingos.
listening.meaning: We get up very late on Sundays.

listening.text: Mi padre se ducha por la noche.
listening.meaning: My father has a shower at night.

listening.text: Me lavo la cara con agua fría.
listening.meaning: I wash my face with cold water.
listening.note: New word: la cara = the face.

listening.text: Os acostáis muy tarde todos los días.
listening.meaning: You all go to bed very late every day.

listening.text: Me duermo en el sofá después de cenar.
listening.meaning: I fall asleep on the sofa after dinner.
listening.note: New word: cenar = to have dinner.

listening.text: Mi hermano se viste rápido y sale de casa a las ocho.
listening.meaning: My brother gets dressed quickly and leaves the house at eight.
listening.note: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: se viste.

conversations.title: Morning people
conversations.scenario: Julia and Andrés compare their mornings.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What time do you get up?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me despierto a las seis, pero me levanto a las siete.
lines.meaning: I wake up at six, but I get up at seven.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué temprano! Yo me levanto a las ocho y media.
lines.meaning: So early! I get up at half past eight.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me ducho, me visto y desayuno en cinco minutos.
lines.meaning: I shower, get dressed and have breakfast in five minutes.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yo me lavo los dientes y salgo sin desayunar.
lines.meaning: I brush my teeth and leave without breakfast.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y por la noche? Yo me acuesto a las once.
lines.meaning: And at night? I go to bed at eleven.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me acuesto tarde y me duermo en el sofá.
lines.meaning: I go to bed late and fall asleep on the sofa.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Entonces, ¿cómo se llama tu sofá? ¡Es tu cama!
lines.meaning: So, what's your sofa's name? It's your bed!

bites.title: Mirror verbs
bites.rule: A -se verb turns the action back on you: levantarse = to get yourself up. Drop the -se and put the matching pronoun in front of the verb.

bites.title: Me, te, se, nos, os, se
bites.rule: Say it aloud: me te se, nos os se. Yo takes me, tú te, nosotros nos, and both él and ellos share se.

bites.title: Los dientes, not mis
bites.rule: The pronoun already says whose body it is, so body parts take the article: me lavo los dientes, never mis dientes.

bites.title: Before or attached
bites.rule: With an infinitive, the pronoun goes before the first verb or attaches to the end: me voy a levantar = voy a levantarme. Never in the middle.
bites.example_meaning: I'm going to go to bed late.

sorts.title: Which pronoun?
sorts.why: The pronoun matches the subject: yo me, tú te, nosotros nos, and él/ella/ellos all use se.

sorts.title: Pronoun or not?
sorts.why: Routine verbs you do to yourself (levantarse, vestirse, acostarse, llamarse) take a pronoun; desayunar, salir and estudiar don't.

sorts.title: Which stem change?
sorts.why: Me despierto (e → ie), me visto (e → i), me acuesto and me duermo (o → ue).

spots.sentence: Yo se levanto a las siete.
Nosotros se acostamos a las once.

spots.why: Body parts take the article with reflexive verbs: los dientes.
Acostarse is o → ue in yo: me acuesto.

spots.sentence: Me vesto rápido por la mañana.
spots.why: Vestirse is e → i: me visto.

builds.meaning: I'm going to get up early.
